meta.location: Zarahemla, the land Bountiful, and the land northward
principles: The record handed on twice in four years

world_behind.title: The record changes hands twice
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has Shiblon receiving the sacred things from Helaman's estate, and verse 11 has him passing them to Helaman's son before his own death.

world_behind.title: Moroni dies in a single clause
world_behind.text: Verse 3 reports it between the record's transfer and the migration north, with no summary of his life. Alma 48:17 had already given the assessment.

world_behind.title: The migration north is large
world_behind.text: Verse 4 counts five thousand four hundred men, with wives and children, leaving Zarahemla in one year.

world_behind.title: Hagoth is described by one adjective
world_behind.text: Verse 5 calls him exceedingly curious, and the record gives no further account of him.

world_behind.title: The ships are placed by the narrow neck
world_behind.text: Verse 5 puts the shipyard on the borders of Bountiful, by Desolation, on the west sea.

world_behind.title: Mormon marks what he does not know
world_behind.text: Verse 8 says the second voyage was never heard of again, calls the drowning a supposition, and says of another ship that its destination is unknown.

world_behind.title: Alma's restriction on the record stands
world_behind.text: Verse 12 says the engravings went out among the people, apart from the parts Alma had commanded should not go forth.

words.text: To walk straight, without deviation. The record uses the word six times, including of Alma the elder at Mosiah 18:29 and of Helaman's armies at Alma 53:21. It is the whole description Shiblon receives.
Treated at 1 Nephi 16:10, of the workmanship of the Liahona. In that sense the word describes skill and fine making. Applied to Hagoth, it credits him with the ships rather than with wondering.
Killed by water. The record uses it eight times, at the Red Sea in 1 Nephi 17:27 and at the destruction in 3 Nephi 8:9 among others. Here it appears inside a sentence that calls itself a supposition.
Treated at Mosiah 28:20, of the plates handed to Alma. The word marks a formal transfer of custody, and this chapter has one on either side of Shiblon's death.
The characters cut into metal plates, and the writing so made. The record uses the word thirteen times, first at 1 Nephi 4:24. Verse 12 reports that they were copied out and circulated.
Treated at Alma 47:36, of Nephites who joined the Lamanites. The war block ends the way it began, with dissenters stirring the Lamanites to anger.

phrases.term: Shiblon took possession of those sacred things which had been delivered unto Helaman by Alma
phrases.text: The line of custody stated in one sentence: Alma to Helaman, Helaman to Shiblon. Alma 37 records the charge that started it.

phrases.term: He was a just man, and he did walk uprightly before God
phrases.text: Shiblon's entire character sketch. Alma 38 had commended him for steadiness, and the record adds that his brother was the same.

phrases.term: And it came to pass that Moroni died also
phrases.text: Six words for the man who occupied twenty chapters. Alma 62:43 had already retired him to his house.

phrases.term: Hagoth, he being an exceedingly curious man
phrases.text: The only thing the record says about him. He builds ships, launches them, and leaves the account.

phrases.term: Launched it forth into the west sea, by the narrow neck which led into the land northward
phrases.text: The one use of "launched" in the record. The location joins two of the book's landmarks, the west sea and the narrow neck.

phrases.term: They were never heard of more. And we suppose that they were drowned in the depths of the sea
phrases.text: Mormon separates the fact from the inference in consecutive sentences. The disappearance is reported; the drowning is offered as a guess.

phrases.term: Whither she did go we know not
phrases.text: A second ship, and a plain statement of ignorance. The record declines to fill the gap.

phrases.term: Corianton had gone forth to the land northward in a ship, to carry forth provisions
phrases.text: The last the record says of Alma's third son. Alma 42:31 had sent him to preach, and this verse has him supplying colonists.

phrases.term: Save it were those parts which had been commanded by Alma should not go forth
phrases.text: The engravings circulate with a reserved portion. The restriction was laid down in Alma 37 and is still being kept forty years later.

phrases.term: Handed down from one generation to another
phrases.text: The rule the whole chapter demonstrates. Two transfers happen in thirteen verses, and both are made before the holder dies.

phrases.term: Thus ended the account of Alma, and Helaman his son, and also Shiblon, who was his son
phrases.text: The book closes by naming three record-keepers in descent. The wars, the missions, and the sermons are gathered under those three names.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: The record passes, and Moroni dies
verses.text: Shiblon takes the sacred things in the thirty-sixth year. He is a just man who walks uprightly and does good continually, and his brother likewise. Moroni dies, and the year ends.

verses.label: v. 4–6
verses.title: The migration and the first ship
verses.text: In the thirty-seventh year five thousand four hundred men with families leave Zarahemla for the land northward. Hagoth, an exceedingly curious man, builds a large ship on the borders of Bountiful by Desolation and launches it into the west sea by the narrow neck. Many Nephites sail north with provisions.

verses.label: v. 7–9
verses.title: More ships, and the record's limit
verses.text: In the thirty-eighth year Hagoth builds more ships. The first returns, takes on more people and provisions, and sails again. Those are never heard of again, and Mormon supposes they drowned. Another ship's destination is unknown. Many others go north by land.

verses.label: v. 10–13
verses.title: Shiblon dies and the record passes again
verses.text: In the thirty-ninth year Shiblon dies, with Corianton away in the north carrying provisions. Shiblon confers the sacred things on Helaman's son, also named Helaman. The engravings had been sent out among the people, apart from the reserved parts, and the sacred things are to be handed down.

verses.label: v. 14–16
verses.title: A last attack
verses.text: Dissenters who had gone over to the Lamanites stir them to anger. A numerous army comes against Moronihah and is beaten and driven back with great loss, and the thirty-ninth year ends.

verses.label: v. 17
verses.title: The account closes
verses.text: Mormon ends the account of Alma, Helaman his son, and Shiblon his son.

chapter.title: The chapter is a series of handoffs
chapter.text: The record moves twice, the army moved to Moronihah in Alma 62:43, and the judgment-seat is already back with Pahoran. Mormon closes the book by showing custody changing cleanly.

chapter.title: Great men are buried in short sentences
chapter.text: Moroni gets six words in verse 3, Shiblon a clause in verse 10. The record spends its praise elsewhere, at Alma 48:17 and Alma 63:2.

chapter.title: Shiblon is described only by conduct
chapter.text: Just, upright, doing good continually, keeping commandments. The record gives him no office and no episode.

chapter.title: Mormon labels his own guess
chapter.text: Verse 8 says "we suppose" about the drowning and "we know not" about the other ship. The report of the disappearance and the explanation for it are kept apart.

chapter.title: The land northward opens as the record closes
chapter.text: Thousands go by land and by sea in three years. Helaman 3 will follow that migration where this chapter stops.

chapter.title: The reserved portion is still reserved
chapter.text: Verse 12 has the engravings published with an exception that Alma set in Alma 37. Two custodians later, the exception holds.

chapter.title: The war ends the way it started
chapter.text: Verse 14 has dissenters stirring the Lamanites to anger, the same mechanism Mormon described at Alma 43:4 and Alma 47.

chapter.title: The book is named for a line, not a man
chapter.text: Verse 17 closes the account of Alma, Helaman, and Shiblon together. Sixty-three chapters are filed under three keepers of one record.

applications.title: Hand it on before you have to
applications.text: Shiblon conferred the record before his death rather than leaving it to be found. Decide now who takes what you are carrying.

applications.title: Say "we suppose" when you are supposing
applications.text: Mormon reported the disappearance as fact and the drowning as a guess. Keeping the two apart in one sentence is a skill worth practicing.

applications.title: Let a good record be short
applications.text: Shiblon's whole life fits in one verse about how he walked. Being described accurately matters more than being described at length.

applications.title: Keep the restriction you were given
applications.text: Alma's limit on the record was still honored two custodians later. Confidences outlive the person who asked for them.

questions.text: What have I been handed that I did not earn?
If my life were summarized in one sentence about conduct, what would it say?
Whose death have I passed over without reckoning?
What am I curious enough about to build?
What am I stating as fact that is actually a supposition?
What would happen to my responsibilities if I stopped tomorrow?
What has someone asked me to keep back, and am I keeping it?
